subject: Ownership liveness and task-admission scale pass

changes: liveness measured against observed network progress, not the local tick
bounded announce / checkpoint / grant gossip instead of per-tick rebroadcast
proposal retried only when the bid set grows
admission frontier derived from membership (floor(N/2)) instead of 1

rootCause: isLive() compares a peer's last observed heartbeat tick against the receiver's OWN logical tick, with a 6-tick window. A healthy peer's heartbeat is only delivered through the Fast DDS bridge, so when the transport backs up the peer looks dead even though it is running.

rootCauseDetail.summary: isLive() compares a peer's last observed heartbeat tick against the receiver's OWN logical tick, with a 6-tick window. A healthy peer's heartbeat is only delivered through the Fast DDS bridge, so when the transport backs up the peer looks dead even though it is running.
rootCauseDetail.selfDeliveryIsSynchronous: OwnershipPeer.send() also calls receive() locally, so a peer always sees its own heartbeat at age 0. Only remote heartbeats traverse the bridge. The measurement shows self at age 0 and every remote peer at age 8-211, which isolates the fault to remote delivery rather than the protocol clock.
rootCauseDetail.notPhysicalExecution: The same failure reproduces with the grid executor and no Nav2 action at all (baseline-dds-*), and does NOT reproduce over UDP at the same N (baseline-udp-*). Nav2 serialised execution is therefore not the cause.
rootCauseDetail.tickRateIsTheHiddenVariable: Because the failure is transport-throughput-bound, whether a given N passes depends on how slowly its ticks happen to run. N=6 Nav2 passed only because Nav2 actions throttled the tick rate below the transport ceiling; at N=7/N=8 no ownership was ever formed, so no Nav2 action ran, ticks ran fast, message rate rose, and the fleet locked into a backlog it could never drain.
rootCauseDetail.volumeDriver: Every peer re-announced EVERY known task on EVERY tick. The receiver ignores an announce for a task it already has, so this is pure waste, and it makes per-tick traffic O(N^2 x tasks): at N=8 with 8 tasks that is ~504 Fast DDS publications per tick.
rootCauseDetail.measuredTransportCeiling: N=8 DDS + grid: settle 8ms -> remote lag 105-140 ticks (unbounded backlog); settle 25ms -> lag 8-9 ticks; settle 116ms -> lag 4 ticks and all peers live. Lag is a direct function of message rate.

fastDdsCompletionByN.transport: Fast DDS (UDPv4, no shared memory, no broker)

peerFailureDetection.mechanism: consecutive ticks without peer heartbeat, measured on observed network progress
peerFailureDetection.note: unchanged; the liveness clock is now robust to transport backlog rather than the window being widened

safetyCounters.invariant: For every task, live peers allowed to execute <= 1; and 0 when quorum is unreachable (except N=1).

fastDds.transport: Fast DDS (UDPv4, no shared memory, no broker)

ddsN8.note: Traffic is per-peer outbound ownership messages. Fast DDS fans each broadcast out once per recipient, so mesh-wide delivery is roughly (N-1) x per-peer sends.

knownRemainingLimitations: Admission is still bounded by one ownership generation per certification round; a task that loses its auction retries next generation.
commRange remains 6, so large fleets are effectively fully connected and per-tick cost still grows toward O(N^2).
Fast DDS throughput, not the protocol, is now the wall: N=8 completes with margin, but per-tick traffic is still O(N^2) in broadcasts and a much larger fleet would need transport work.
No hardware validation; Nav2 remains a simulated continuous world with a shared logical clock.
